    How to make a mandala SVG for Cricut

    1. Design it. Draw in the maker above, or pick a template and change it.
    2. Choose Cut-ready shapes. In Download, set SVG to Cut-ready shapes, then enter the width and a line thickness for your material.
    3. Download the SVG. The maker merges overlapping lines into clean shapes and tells you if anything will come out as loose pieces.
    4. Upload to Design Space. Choose Upload, then Upload Image, pick the SVG, and add it to your canvas.

    Tips for clean cuts

    • Keep it connected. Floating dots and shapes cut out as separate pieces. Overlap shapes with the ring next to them, or add a ring through them.
    • Size first, then thickness. The SVG opens at the width you entered. If you resize it a lot in Design Space, the line thickness changes too.
    • Test on scrap. Intricate mandalas push a cutting mat's grip. Cut a small version first.
    • Use a stencil for paint. The Stencil option cuts the design out of a solid disc, which works for stencil vinyl and painting. Closed areas fall out of a stencil, so the maker counts them for you.

    Prefer a ready-made design? Start from the flower mandala or the geometric mandala template.

    Questions

    What's the difference between Cut-ready shapes and Line drawing?

    A line drawing is made of strokes, which Cricut Design Space treats as thin outlines. Cut-ready shapes turn every line into a solid shape with the thickness you choose, so the machine cuts around it and the design comes out in one piece.

    What line thickness should I use?

    For cardstock and vinyl, try 0.04 to 0.08 inches at a 10 to 12 inch size. Thinner lines look more delicate but tear more easily when you weed or lift them.

    Can I make a layered 3D mandala?

    Yes. Make a few versions of a design with more detail removed in each one, export each as a cut-ready SVG at the same size, and cut each in a different color of cardstock. Stack them with foam dots between layers.
